<action type="say">
The system is clear that this order can’t be canceled anymore: it’s already shipped, and all items are marked ineligible for cancellation. I don’t have any way to override that or directly intercept the package from here.

What you can usually do in this situation (depending on the retailer/carrier policies):

1) **Ask the retailer’s support about a “carrier intercept”**  
   - Some carriers (e.g., UPS/FedEx) support delivery intercept/redirect, but it has to be initiated by the sender (the retailer), not the recipient.  
   - If the retailer offers it, they may be able to have the package returned to them in transit. In practice this is almost always processed as a **return** (refund after the item is back with them), not a pre-ship cancellation, but it can save you from handling the item.

2) **Refuse delivery at the door (if possible)**  
   - If the package requires a signature, you can tell the driver you’re refusing the package. It is then sent back to the sender.  
   - If it doesn’t require a signature, some carriers still treat “refused – return to sender” scans similarly when you mark it as refused right away.  
   - Again, this is usually processed as a **return-to-sender refund**, not a pure cancellation, but it often means you don’t have to initiate a standard return yourself.

3) **If neither is available, do a standard return once delivered**  
   - This is the option I can directly help you with in this system: once the tracking shows it delivered, we can set up a return label and you’ll get a refund after it’s received and processed.

If you’d like, tell me:
- whether the retailer offers any “intercept” option in your account/shipping email, or  
- whether you expect to be home for delivery (to try refusing at the door),

and I can help you decide the simplest path and then handle the return side here as soon as it’s eligible.</action>
